ytTitle: Claude Is Coding Blind (One Flag Fixes It: claude --chrome)
caption:
Claude built your login page. It has never seen it.

It writes the button, tells you it works, and ships it without ever opening the page. One flag fixes that:

claude --chrome

Claude Code connects to the Claude in Chrome extension and opens your app in a real, visible Chrome window. It clicks the buttons, fills the forms and reads the console errors, then fixes the code and checks again.

It also uses the sites you're already logged into (Gmail, Notion, your dashboards), with no connectors to set up. When it hits a login page or a CAPTCHA, it stops and hands it back to you.

The catch: it needs a paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise) signed in with /login, and the browser tools eat context. Leave it off by default and add the flag when you need it.

Setup:
1. Install the Claude in Chrome extension from the Chrome Web Store
2. Run claude --chrome
3. Type /chrome to check it says Enabled

ytTitle: Your Vibe-Coded App Can Get Fined Before Its First Sale
caption:
Your vibe-coded app can rack up fines before it makes a single sale. Four to check before launch:

1. Kids under 13 sign up and you keep their data (COPPA). US civil penalties go up to $53,088 per violation. Fix: an age gate on sign-up.
2. Fonts loaded straight from Google send every visitor's IP to Google. In January 2022 a Munich court ordered one site to pay a visitor €100 under GDPR. Fix: self-host your fonts.
3. Session replay recording visitors without consent. California's wiretap law (CIPA) allows $5,000 per violation, and lawyers are suing over it. Fix: no recording or tracking until they consent.
4. Marketing emails with no unsubscribe link or postal address (CAN-SPAM). Up to $53,088 per email. Fix: add both to every send.

The one prompt: "Audit this app for legal exposure and fix what you find: age gate on sign-up, self-host all fonts, no session replay or tracking before consent, unsubscribe link and postal address in every email. List each change you made."

Not legal advice. If real money is on the line, talk to a lawyer.

Stop being the courier.

caption:

ytTitle: Claude Read 4 of Your 40 Files (Hot Repo of the Week: Open Code Review)
caption:
Claude reviewed your 40-file pull request. It read four of them.

Hot repo of the week: alibaba/open-code-review, almost 10,000 new GitHub stars in seven days.

It's the AI code reviewer Alibaba ran internally for two years across tens of thousands of developers, now open source (Apache-2.0).

Why it's different: hard-coded rules decide which files get reviewed, so nothing gets skipped, and the AI only does the judging. On Alibaba's own benchmark, using the same model as Claude Code, it raised fewer false alarms on about a ninth of the tokens. The trade-off, in their words: it catches fewer issues overall, in exchange for less noise.

Setup:
npm install -g @alibaba-group/open-code-review
ocr review

Or let Claude Code run the review itself with delegate mode (ocr delegate), no extra API key needed.

github.com/alibaba/open-code-review

ytTitle: Your Claude Code Has Zero Safety Nets. Add These 4
caption:
Your Claude Code has zero safety nets. Fit these four before it deletes something.

1. Checkpoints: double-tap Esc (or /rewind) to restore the code, the chat, or both.
2. Git: commit before big changes. Checkpoints only track Claude's own edits, so they don't replace git.
3. Hooks: block what must never happen. Hooks are guaranteed, CLAUDE.md is only advice.
4. /sandbox: sandboxed commands run walled off, without asking you every time.

Screenshot this. Set them up before you need them.

ytTitle: Claude Code Does One Job at a Time. Run Four Instead
caption:
Your Claude Code does one job at a time. Here's how to run four.

1. Skills: write a workflow once in .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, then run it with /<name>.
2. claude -p: pipe a file straight in from the terminal, e.g. cat error.log | claude -p "what broke?"
3. Worktrees: separate sessions in separate git checkouts, so edits never collide.
4. /batch: one instruction, split across up to 30 subagents.

Start with skills. They're the easiest win.

note: MEMORY - 0/4 meter series (four verified plugs), cream-stage bots, Harrison ElevenLabs, built 2026-10-05.
ytTitle: Claude Forgets Everything. Plug In These 4
caption:
Claude forgets everything between sessions. Unless you plug in these four.

1. /init: generates a starter CLAUDE.md from your project. Claude reads it at the start of every conversation.
2. Keep it short: for each line ask "would Claude mess up without this?" If not, cut it.
3. claude --continue: back into your last conversation. (claude --resume to pick an older one.)
4. Checkpoints save with the conversation, so you can close the terminal, resume later and still rewind.

Set it up once. Stop re-explaining.
